title: Exact Expressions of Entropy for Classical Non-interacting Many-body Systems
authors: Yuheng Wu, Henrik Heelweg, Rigel Galgana
abstract: In the thermodynamic limit, the equilibrium state of a many-body system can be characterized by three pairs of conjugate thermodynamic variables: $E/T,V/P,N/μ$. In this limit, the thermodynamic properties in all ensembles are equivalent up to the leading order of $E,V,N$. However, for systems of finite size, this ensemble equivalence is no longer exact, and the thermodynamic properties may differ substantially among ensembles. To quantify these finite-size effects rigorously, it is desirable to develop a universal ensemble theory applicable to systems of arbitrary size, providing exact expressions for entropy and, thereby, giving rise to the precise value of all equilibrium thermodynamic quantities. In this work, we propose a theory that determines the exact entropy expressions for classical non-interacting many-body systems of arbitrary size across all statistical ensembles, based on only two postulates: \textbf{stationarity}, requiring that the physical laws be invariant under time translation, and \textbf{unbiasedness}, requiring that the equilibrium mixed state maximize the entropy subject to the prescribed constraints. Moreover, we show that the entropy expressions obtained in different ensembles converge to the common asymptotic form $S \asymp \ln\!\left( \left( \frac{4πm e E}{3N} \right)^{3N/2} \cdot \left(\frac{V}{N}\right)^N \right)+N$, consistent with the predictions of the large deviation theory.
summary: This work develops a universal statistical mechanics theory to calculate the exact entropy for finite classical many-body systems across all relevant ensembles. By applying maximum entropy principles based on two core physical postulates, the authors show that while ensemble properties differ at small sizes, they converge correctly to established thermodynamic limits. This provides a rigorous framework for understanding finite-size effects in statistical physics.
main_problem: To develop a universal ensemble theory that provides exact expressions for entropy for classical non-interacting many-body systems, resolving discrepancies in thermodynamic properties among different ensembles when the system is finite.
main_result: The derived entropy expressions across various statistical ensembles are shown to converge asymptotically to a common limit in the thermodynamic limit, confirming ensemble equivalence while rigorously quantifying finite-size corrections.
method: The theory uses maximum entropy optimization based on two postulates: stationarity and unbiasedness, applied to four representative thermodynamic ensembles.
model_or_system: The system is modeled as classical non-interacting many-body particles governed by a simple quadratic Hamiltonian (L = sum(p_i^2/2m)).
key_observables: Entropy (S), Temperature (T), Pressure (P), Chemical Potential (mu), and the ensemble-dependent intensive variables.
important_parameters: System size (N, V), Energy (E), and the thermodynamic limit ($N 	o \infty$).
main_assumptions: The system is assumed to be a regular Hamiltonian system, and the analysis relies on extending beyond the standard thermodynamic limit approximation.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematics illustrate the state space constraints for four representative ensembles. Figure 2 illustrates the ensemble dependence of intensive variables like chemical potential ($\partial S / \partial N$).
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the need for a universal theory to address finite-size effects, then derives exact entropy expressions for four key ensembles using maximum entropy principles, and finally proves the asymptotic equivalence of these results in the thermodynamic limit.
why_interesting: While focused on classical systems, establishing rigorous, non-asymptotic ensemble equivalence is foundational. The methodology of deriving fundamental quantities from minimal postulates (stationarity/unbiasedness) has parallels in defining quantum equilibrium states.
